title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (March 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes after one 301) — "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-03-30 is the last Tuesday of March 2027. The rule is corroborated for MARCH specifically by three of the publisher's own dated next-release lines, each fetched direct 2026-09-06 at HTTP 200 from a page verified against its own "Source: February <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line, and each naming that year's last Tuesday of March: CCI-Feb-2023 "The next release is Tuesday, March 28 at 10 AM ET", CCI-Feb-2024 "Tuesday, March 26th", CCI-Feb-2025 "Tuesday, March 25th" — the last of which is confirmed by CCI-Mar-2025's own "Updated: 2025-03-25". No March-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a verified March record rather than a posted date. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-02-23 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), one edition forward on the same chain by which 01-26 proposed 02-23. Proposed for a concrete reason rather than bookkeeping: it is the REPLICATION INSTANCE for the proposer's central finding. That ledger measured the de-confounded control -- of 68 rule-derived CB release days since 2021, the 51 with no FOMC collision differ from baseline on 0 of 9 instruments with no near-miss, and clean-vs-collision head to head is also 0 of 9 -- and registered FT-consumer-confidence-2027-02-23-2 to re-run that pipeline after 2027-06-30 with 2027's clean prints added. Per the Fed's own posted 2027 calendar (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched 2026-09-06 HTTP 200: Jan 26-27, Mar 16-17, Apr 27-28, Jun 8-9, Jul 27-28, Sep 14-15, Oct 26-27, Dec 7-8), 2027-03-30 is clean -- it is 13 days after the March 16-17 decision -- and it is one of exactly four clean prints in the scoring window, so the forward test cannot be scored without it. Second reason: it is the FIRST edition whose panel opens after the March SEP meeting, making it the first consumer read of the post-decision regime. Note for whichever lane takes it: Good Friday falls on 2027-03-26 (good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, tracked), four days before this print, so the field window straddles a holiday-shortened week. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
